_about: Checks excluded from the nightly vendored-spec run. No-silent-caps: every entry carries a reason, and this file is SHARED WITH THE VERIFICATION TEAM for agreement (their review condition 2-2); an exclusion is a spec/seed gap to resolve, not a way to make the gate green. Keys: modules.<name> excludes a whole module; checks."<module>:<tc>" excludes one check. History: this file carried twenty-one entries until 2026-08-13, all resolved at the source rather than carved out (eleven expected 403 where existence-hiding returns 404, five encoded behaviour the guides settled the other way, three bound to the original campaign's environment, one spec regex defect, one needing a Beat-only backup the nightly workflow now triggers itself). It stayed empty until 2026-09-06, when TC-INTG-05-000-secret-setup was added back for a genuine target-evolution gap (see that entry). Add entries back only with a reason that says which category applies: source-resolved behaviour difference, campaign-environment binding, spec defect, or target evolution pending upstream re-keying.

checks.integrations:TC-INTG-05-000-secret-setup: Target evolution: migrations 0084-0086 (PR #379) moved projects.webhook_secret from a plaintext column to an encrypted webhook_secret_encrypted column as an expand-migrate-contract sequence, then dropped the plaintext column. The product is correct; the spec's raw-SQL precondition still references the dropped column, and the gitlab branch's literal-value comparison can't be reproduced against Fernet ciphertext anyway. Re-keying requested from the verification team: https://github.com/haksungjang/bug-hunter/issues/20. Covered on our side by apps/backend/tests/integration/test_seed_verify_baseline_webhook_secrets.py, which asserts the demo seed populates webhook_secret_encrypted for both fixtures.
